newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rebounds as NY rallies on weather.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rebounds as NY rallies on weather.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures rebounded from their early losses to end Monday higher after a muted session.
Traders said the gains followed a rally in New York after Brazil's local weathermen forecast colder weather for Brazil's coffee belt this weekend.
A significant polar air mass might pass the coffee areas from the evening of July 5 which could represent the greatest frost threat seen so far this year, meteorologists Somar said.
But some U.S. forecasters said although a cooler weather was expected, no crop-damaging frost was seen.
Activity in London's robusta futures was dominated by July/Sept switches as players rolled forward the July positions before the contract's first tender day on Tuesday.
The day's volume was 5,576 lots, with July and September accounting for more than 4,600.
Traders also noted light trade covering and scale-down roaster buying which helped values recover from early losses.
Benchmark September, which spent the afternoon languishing in the $1,780-$1,790 range, rose to the day's peak of $1,815 in late business on New York's rise before closing $14 up at $1,797.
"There have been some last minute July/Sept switch trades before the first notice day," said one. The spread widened to end at $32 from Friday's close at $15.
July's uncovered positions stood at 3,287 lots by the close of business on Friday, down 613 from a day earlier.

Traders said Friday's U.S. Department of Agriculture's world coffee supply/demand estimates contained in its latest semi-annual Tropical Products: World Markets and Trade report were described as neutral.
But they noted a sharp downward revision in Indonesia's 1997/98 coffee crop to 4.6 million bags from 6.1 million previously.
Chartwise, analysts said LIFFE coffee should hold this month's range for the time being, but bearish chart indicators may soon start to pressure benchmark September lower.
